To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a Tunisian dialect SA model which outperforms other dialects or MSLA models.

the performance of the best SA model trained on the MSA or multi dialectal data sets is 0.67 and 0.69 respectively, and that the performance of SA model trained on Tunisian Dialect data set is 0.75, showing an improvement of 0.06 and 0.06 over the best model trained with MSA or Multi dialectal data set respectively.

we built and released a corpus of Tunisian dialect comments annotated with sentiment polarity, and that we showed that this corpus is more effective in training a sentiment analysis system than the existing MSA and other dialectal Arabic resources.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) the creation of a Tunisian dialect dataset; (ii) a comparison of the performances of SA systems trained on different Arabic dialects and MSA; (iii) an analysis of the linguistic characteristics of Tunisian dialect that may affect the performances of SA.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our proposed system outperforms all the previous works that were conducted in this field, and that our proposed approach is a very promising one, and it can be used as a baseline for further research in this domain.

the proposed system has been tested on a large dataset of Tunisian dialect, and has achieved a high accuracy rate of 85.6% for the classification of Tunisian dialect comments into negative and positive classes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to perform SA on Tunisian dialect and we show that it is possible to achieve good results using freely available data.
we have built a Tunisian Sentiment Corpus and trained several models to determine the sentiment polarity of comments in Tunisian dialect.
We have developed a Tunisian dialect sentiment analysis system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of dialect-specific data sets can significantly boost the performance of SA systems for Tunisian dialect.
a corpus of a given Arabic dialect can be used to train a SA system for the same dialect.
a corpus of Tunisian dialect is needed to train a sentiment analysis system for the Tunisian dialect.
